title: Flux-based machine learning predicts antibiotic combination interactions in E. coli
summary: A random forest trained on genome-scale metabolic model flux profiles predicted antibiotic synergy (AUROC 0.83) and antagonism (AUROC 0.98) for E. coli across 57 metabolic conditions, based on experimental measurements. Flux entropy was predictive, population flux balance analysis suggested two subpopulations defined by eno, fadB and fabD, and 24 robustly synergistic combinations were nominated. The subpopulation and synergy nominations are model-derived and not all were tested; a 2021 preprint exists whose version was not compared.
ai_technology: Random forest (CARAMeL) trained on genome-scale metabolic model flux profiles

evidence.tested: Experimental Biolog-based growth and interaction measurements in E. coli across 57 conditions.
evidence.unknown: Experimental confirmation of nominated combinations; the M. tuberculosis model was not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts drug interaction outcomes from flux profiles

source_review.scope: Abstract and Europe PMC full-text Methods/Results excerpts read. Publisher version not otherwise accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
